ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before formation, every UBO, director, officer, authorized signatory, and material shareholder must be screened under a risk-based approach against the UN Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK OFSI Consolidated List, Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs and KoFIU domestic designations, and the FATF High-Risk and Non-Cooperative Jurisdictions List. PEP status of foreign and domestic political figures, immediate family members, and close associates must be checked on an ongoing basis. Positive hits require escalated approval, source-of-funds evidence, and immediate rejection for any sanctions match. Screening records must be preserved for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (I-ONE) and its trade-name search engine
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Korean Commercial Act Article 19 and the Commercial Registration Rules, the registered name of a Yuhan Hoesa limited liability company must be presented in the local script; foreign-language elements must be phonetically transliterated into the local Hangul script. The four-tier naming convention requires (1) a distinctive trade-name element, (2) a transliterated foreign brand where applicable, (3) a permissible business-purpose descriptor, and (4) the legal-form suffix Yuhan Hoesa. An English trade name may be registered only as a secondary trade name and cannot replace the formal registered name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry rejects a proposed name, the applicant must first preserve the rejection notice and upload a corrective application through the I-ONE portal. Within 14 days of the rejection, a written objection may be filed with the registration officer stating the statutory basis for the name, attaching a fresh name-search certificate and amended articles. If the officer sustains the rejection, the applicant may file an immediate appeal to the competent district court under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act. Alternatively, for a sensitive token, the applicant may seek prior ministerial approval from the responsible authority or abandon the token and refile.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox may be acceptable for a purely administrative registered address only if the local municipal tax office accepts it and a physical service-management arrangement exists. For this specific medical-device manufacturing entity, however, a virtual office is insufficient and will be rejected by the National Tax Service, MFDS, customs, and banking institutions. The entity must maintain an actual commercial place of business where books, records, board minutes, corporate seal, manufacturing assets, and medical-device license documentation are physically present. A virtual address may be used only as an auxiliary communication address and cannot serve as the sole registered office, manufacturing site, or tax-compliance address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) post a visible company sign at the registered office; (2) maintain physical books, corporate seal, and minutes at the registered office; (3) keep an actual MFDS-licensed manufacturing facility aligned with the medical-device business; (4) ensure VAT invoices, customs declarations, tax filings, and bank account statements use the registered address; (5) be prepared to answer unannounced National Tax Service and municipal tax office site visits. Quantified risk: for a registered medical-device manufacturing entity, unannounced physical inspection risk is moderate, estimated at 20-30% within the first 12 months; the risk increases to 50-70% if a virtual office is used as the sole registered address; for a non-manufacturing entity the risk would be approximately 5-10%.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Chapter IV 'Limited Liability Company', Articles 287 through 287-74, together with the Presidential Decree on Commercial Registration and the Commercial Registration Rules of the Supreme Court.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Section of the District Court Registration Office having jurisdiction over the company's registered office and the Internet Registration Office (IRO) operated by the Supreme Court of South Korea.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Articles of Incorporation (Jeonggwan) and Application for Incorporation Registration of a Limited Liability Company under Article 287-39 of the Commercial Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. South Korean law imposes no statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Yuhan Hoesa. However, the full amount of subscribed capital must be paid into a domestic bank account in the company-in-formation name before registration, and the bank's certificate of paid-in capital must be submitted. No blocked or escrowed capital account is required for foreign investors, but the paid-in amount must be identifiable as foreign investment if invested by non-residents.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF YUHANG HOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY). WHEREAS the Company has been formed under the Limited Liability Company provisions of the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Articles 287 through 287-74; WHEREAS the Articles of Incorporation have been duly executed, subscribed by the initial member, and are stated to be effective upon incorporation; WHEREAS the principal objects of the Company are the manufacture, vapor deposition, assembly, testing, export, distribution, and repair of amorphous silicon cesium iodide digital X-ray flat panel detectors, DR detector panels, related medical imaging hardware, and associated engineering and OEM services; WHEREAS the initial capital has been subscribed by the founding member as set out in the Articles of Incorporation; NOW, THEREFORE, the sole incorporator and initial director, duly convened in organizational meeting, hereby resolves, and such resolutions are adopted unanimously as the first minutes of the Company: 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. The total subscribed capital of the Company, comprising the number of participation units stated in the Articles of Incorporation at the agreed issue price, is hereby ratified, fully subscribed, allotted, and paid in cash. The capital contribution account opened for this purpose at a licensed bank in the Republic of Korea, and the certificate of paid-in capital issued by such bank, are adopted as conclusive evidence of payment. The representative director is directed to record the paid-in capital in the Company's book of accounts and to apply the funds solely to the lawful business purposes of the Company. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The corporate banking relationship and current account opened with the domestic banking institution identified in the board packet are hereby approved. The Representative Director, the Chief Financial Officer, and any one additional director acting jointly shall be, and are, authorized to open, operate, close, and manage bank accounts, to sign checks and electronic banking mandates, to apply for documentary credits and trade facilities, to receive Swift transfers and telegraphic wire payments, and to execute foreign exchange contracts necessary for export sales of X-ray detectors and related components. All bank mandates and specimen signature cards are ratified. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. The registered office of the Company is fixed at the address stated in the Articles of Incorporation and recorded in the initial registration application. That office shall be the Company's statutory seat, the place for service of legal process, and the jurisdiction for tax and commercial registration. The directors are authorized to execute or receive a lease, consent to office use, evidence of legal address, and all ancillary documents required by the Court Registration Office. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. The following persons are appointed as first statutory officers: one Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer, who shall be the principal executive; one Chief Financial Officer and Operations Director, who shall supervise treasury, tax filings, and accounting; and one Manufacturing and Industrial Licensing Officer, who shall have responsibility for obtaining all medical device manufacturing licenses, environmental approvals, fire safety permits, and workplace safety certifications. All officers are granted full delegated authority to sign regulatory applications, hire domestic professional advisors, enter into supply and OEM contracts, and take all actions reasonably required to complete Stage 2 statutory formation and industrial licensing. The above resolutions are binding and shall be transcribed into the Company's permanent minutes, signed by the attending director, and dated as of the organizational meeting day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search, Reservation, and Foreign Ownership Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Internet Registration Office (IRO) under the Supreme Court of South Korea; KOTRA/Invest Korea for foreign investment pre-declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The formation attorney must conduct a prior name availability search in Hangul transliteration of Yuhan Hoesa on the Internet Registration Office database to confirm the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to any registered domestic corporate name. Upon preliminary clearance, the attorney must submit an application for name reservation and obtain a certificate of name reservation. Simultaneously, if the sole or contributing shareholder is a foreign entity or non-resident, the attorney must prepare a foreign investment verification file with KOTRA or Invest Korea, including passport or corporate registration evidence, banking AML/KYC declarations, and a power of attorney to the Korean representative. The name reservation is then held secure while the incorporation dossier is completed.
required_dossiers: Application for corporate name reservation
Certificate of name search result and reservation
Passport or national ID copies of each subscribing member
Foreign entity registration certificate or Certificate of Incorporation, if applicable
Notarized or apostilled Power of Attorney appointing the Korean formation attorney
Anti-money-laundering declaration and ultimate beneficial ownership statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry rejects or queries the name for similarity, file a written explanatory objection or select and reserve an alternate name. If the foreign investor's authorization is defective, submit notarized or apostilled corporate resolutions and wait for the Registry's supplementary instruction to be cured before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation, Notarization, and Paid-in Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean Notary Public designated for incorporation matters; Domestic commercial bank authorized to issue capital deposit certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The attorney must prepare Korean-language Articles of Incorporation with a side-by-side English translation. The Articles must state the Company's legal name, principal office, exact purposes covering vapor deposition of amorphous silicon cesium iodide, assembly of digital X-ray flat panel detectors, OEM manufacturing, sale, import/export, and related technical services. The Articles must identify each member, the number of participation units, the value of contributed capital, the method of profit distribution, and the names and duties of initial directors. To evidence capital subscription, the Company must open a bank account under the temporary name of the entity in formation, deposit the subscribed capital, and request a certificate of deposit. All member identification documents must be presented. Thereafter, the formation attorney must deliver the complete Article package to a licensed notary for verification of signatures and legal capacity. The notarized deed and the bank certificate are indispensable prerequisites for incorporation registration.
required_dossiers: Draft and final Korean-language Articles of Incorporation
English translation of the Articles of Incorporation
Bank capital deposit certificate or statement of paid-in capital
Certified copies of individual ID cards or passports of all members
Corporate registry extract of any corporate member
Minutes or written consent appointing the initial directors
Registered office consent or lease contract if available at this stage
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises questions on shareholder authority or corporate purpose, file certified translations, court-style statutory declarations, or corrected articles for re-signature. If the bank refuses to issue the capital certificate because of slight name mismatch, close the account, reopen it under the exact reserved name, and re-deposit the funds before proceeding.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Court Registration of Incorporation and Commercial Registry Extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Section, District Court Registration Office of the registered office; Internet Registration Office (IRO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The attorney must submit the incorporation registration application to the District Court with jurisdiction over the Company's registered office within 14 days of the capital payment, either physically or through the IRO online portal. The application must include the notarized Articles of Incorporation, bank certificate of paid-in capital, directors' written acceptance letters, individual seal certificates, the registered office lease or owner consent, and the completed court-prescribed form signed by all initial directors. After the court registers the Company, the attorney must obtain a Certificate of Registered Matters and an extract of the corporate registry. These documents establish the corporate legal personality of the Yuhan Hoesa and are required for subsequent tax, banking, and licensing steps.
required_dossiers: Application for incorporation registration
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Bank certificate of paid-in capital
Directors' written acceptance of office
Personal seal certificates of each director
Power of attorney filed with the court
Registered office lease agreement or owner's written consent
Individual identification documents of directors and members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a supplementary instruction or requests correction, comply within the prescribed three to five business day cure period. If the application is formally refused, file an objection or application for adjudication with the district court within 15 days of the written refusal; alternatively, amend the Articles and re-submit as a new registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: National Tax Service Registration and Foreign Investment Post-Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) district tax office via HomeTax; KOTRA/Invest Korea foreign investment reporting window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 20 days after court registration, the Company must file a business registration report with the NTS district office having jurisdiction over the registered office. The filing is made online using the Company's corporate registration number, and it must identify the principal place of business, tax representative or CEO, corporate purpose, and expected VAT business. Attach the corporate registry extract, lease contract, director ID copies, and bank account confirmation; the tax office will issue a Business Registration Certificate. If the Member is foreign, the attorney must also file a foreign investment report with KOTRA/Invest Korea within 30 days of fund payment and complete the foreign exchange declaration with the bank receiving the foreign wire transfer. These obligations ensure the Company may lawfully issue sales invoices and enter the Korea electronic tax invoice system.
required_dossiers: Corporate registration certificate covering all registered matters
Application for business registration under the Value-Added Tax Act
Lease agreement for the registered office or factory
Director and representative identification documents
Bank account opening confirmation
Capital contribution receipts and foreign exchange bank confirmation, if applicable
Foreign investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS suspends or returns the business registration application, promptly submit the missing corporate registry extract, lease proof, or identity certificates and re-file through the HomeTax portal. If late filing penalties are proposed, pay under protest, file a correction request, and submit a written explanation to the head of the district tax office within the statutory objection period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial, Medical Device, Environmental, and Fire Safety Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Regional Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) district office; local municipal environmental department under the Ministry of Environment; local Fire Safety Center and KOSHA
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prior to any physical manufacturing operation, the Company must obtain a Medical Device Manufacturing License under the Medical Devices Act and complete KGMP quality management certification for the production of digital X-ray flat panel detectors. The manufacturing facility must undergo an MFDS establishment inspection covering cleanroom class, static control, vapor deposition equipment, assembly lines, and quality documentation. For environmental compliance, the Company must verify the total factory floor area and submit a full or small-scale Environmental Impact Assessment, or an Environmental Registration, to the local municipal environmental authority as applicable; if the factory uses chemicals such as silane, cesium iodide precursors, or liquid scintillators, a pollutant discharge registration and toxic chemical inventory may be required. Concurrently, the local Fire Safety Center must issue a Fire Safety Permit/Civil Defense clearance certificate after inspecting hazardous chemical storage, fire suppression systems, and emergency evacuation plans, and KOSHA must perform a workplace hazard assessment to approve industrial safety compliance.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registered Matters confirming incorporation
Medical device manufacturing license application with product list
Facility layout drawings and cleanroom classification documents
KGMP quality management system manual and SOPs
Equipment list for vapor deposition, panel lamination, and testing
Environmental impact assessment form or environmental registration form
Wastewater, VOC, and hazardous waste management plans
Fire safety layout and civil defense emergency plan
KOSHA chemical hazard assessment and occupational safety certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MFDS refuses or delays the manufacturing license, cure the stated deficiencies, schedule a re-inspection, and resubmit with a corrective action report. If the municipal environmental office scales the EIA category upward, provide enhanced mitigation measures and updated emissions calculations. If fire safety certification is denied, perform all remedial construction and fire protection upgrades required by the local fire officer and request a second inspection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS), Medical Device Safety Bureau; local municipal Economic and Industrial Licensing Division; Ministry of Environment; local Fire Safety Center; Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency (KOSHA)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Medical Device Manufacturing License under the Medical Devices Act and KGMP Certification; Factory Establishment and Registration for Medical Devices Manufacturing

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (MoE) of the Republic of Korea, Korea Environment Corporation (K-eco), and the local municipal environmental agency with factory jurisdiction
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: The production facility using vapor deposition of amorphous silicon cesium iodide and X-ray detector assembly is classified as a physical industrial manufacturing site. A Full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) is required only for projects above 100,000 square meters of factory floor area or located in sensitive watersheds; a Small-Scale Environmental Impact Assessment applies to factories between 10,000 and 100,000 square meters; and an Environmental Registration, small-scale emission registration, or exemption applies below 10,000 square meters depending on local municipal bylaws and chemical usage quantity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharged from the detector production line must comply with the Korean Water Environment Conservation Act: biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) ≤ 30 mg/L, chemical oxygen demand (COD) ≤ 40 mg/L, suspended solids ≤ 30 mg/L, total nitrogen ≤ 20 mg/L, and total phosphorus ≤ 0.5 mg/L for facilities discharging below 5,000 m3/day, with stricter limits inside water source protection zones. VOCs and stack emissions from vapor deposition and baking must comply with the Clean Air Conservation Act: total volatile organic compounds ≤ 50 ppm as carbon equivalent at the emission stack, fugitive odor thresholds for benzene ≤ 0.3 ppm, toluene ≤ 10 ppm, ethylbenzene ≤ 10 ppm, and xylene ≤ 10 ppm under the Odor Prevention Act; particulate matter ≤ 30 mg/Sm3; NOx ≤ 150 ppm; SOx ≤ 20 ppm. Hazardous waste must be segregated, stored with secondary containment, and shipped only to licensed treatment facilities using the electronic manifests and reporting thresholds specified under the Waste Management Act and Chemicals Control Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The Company must obtain a Fire Safety Certificate issued by the local Fire Safety Center under the Framework Act on Fire-Fighting and Prevention covering building occupancy, automatic fire suppression, alarm systems, and hazardous chemical storage; a Civil Defense clearance confirming emergency evacuation planning and underground protective facility compliance; a structural load and occupancy safety inspection for the cleanroom and deposition equipment floor; and a Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency (KOSHA) workplace hazard assessment approving chemical fume ventilation, personal protective equipment, toxic gas monitoring, and radiation shielding for any X-ray test sources.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online filing and e-invoice transmission are performed through the HomeTax electronic tax administration portal. Korea Customs Service (KCS) operates the UNI-PASS system for customs declarations and export clearance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: If the applicant is the foreign non-resident owner of the Yuhan Hoesa and is itself making taxable supplies in Korea, appoint a fiscal tax representative; the Korean domestic Yuhan Hoesa may file directly through its registered office. Step 2: Prepare the certified copy of the Korean articles of incorporation (if filing for the Yuhan Hoesa) or the foreign registration certificate of the foreign entity, powers of attorney, passport or legal ID of the representative, and evidence of the Korean place of business such as a lease or service contract. Step 3: File the application for a Business Registration Number with the District Tax Office having jurisdiction over the Korean registered office, or with the NTS international transaction unit if the applicant is a foreign non-resident with no fixed domestic place of business. Step 4: NTS issues the 10-digit Business Registration Number which functions as the national TIN and VAT registration number. Step 5: Register in HomeTax for electronic tax invoice issuance and open a foreign exchange bank account for export proceeds. Step 6: Apply separately to Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS for the exporter/customs business number. No minimum capital applies to the Yuhan Hoesa and 100% foreign ownership is permitted for the medical device manufacturing scope.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The Yuhan Hoesa is a domestic corporation under the Korean Corporate Tax Act and is taxed at the entity level on its worldwide income; no pass-through or partnership classification is available. Export profit remains in the Korean corporate tax net, while the VAT treatment is independently governed by the VAT Act.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. South Korea does not provide a check-the-box or entity-classification election for locally incorporated Yuhan Hoesa companies. Hybrid mismatch outcomes are constrained by the Korean general anti-avoidance rule and the OECD BEPS Action 2 compliant domestic rules, but no elective filing is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Korean VAT Act, administered nationally by NTS; exports of goods are subject to the 0% zero rate.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: None for a corporate supplier: the Yuhan Hoesa must register for VAT from the commencement of business regardless of turnover, so the effective registration threshold is KRW 0. The KRW 80,000,000 threshold applies only to the simplified taxpayer regime for small natural persons; a company cannot use the simplified threshold and must be a general VAT taxpayer.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic tax invoice (e-tax invoice) transmission through NTS HomeTax. A general VAT taxpayer must issue an electronic tax invoice for every taxable supply and transmit it to NTS no later than the day after the invoice date. South Korea does not use per-invoice digital stamping; instead, NTS applies centralized anti-fraud matching of e-tax invoices with KCS export declarations and foreign exchange bank reports. Direct HomeTax filing or NTS-approved outsourced electronic tax invoice service providers may be used for machine-to-machine submission. Export invoices must be marked as zero-rated supplies and linked to the KCS UNI-PASS export declaration.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of the digital X-ray flat panel detectors qualifies for 0% VAT under the Korean VAT Act when: (a) the goods are sold by the Korean Yuhan Hoesa to a foreign buyer; (b) the goods are declared to Korea Customs Service as an export and physically depart Korea on or before the invoice date; (c) the exporter issues a zero-rated electronic tax invoice; and (d) the export proceeds are received in foreign currency by a Korean foreign exchange bank within the statutory settlement period. Offshore digital services would require separate proof that the service is B2B and consumed outside Korea, but the controlled project scope is physical goods OEM export, so goods-export evidence is the controlling substantiation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Export Declaration and Export Clearance Statement issued in UNI-PASS
Commercial invoice and packing list identifying the goods, HS code, quantity, unit value and foreign buyer
Ocean Bill of Lading or Airway Bill signed by the carrier showing the Korean shipper and foreign consignee
Foreign exchange bank Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or equivalent foreign currency receipt evidence
Zero-rated electronic tax invoice issued through HomeTax for the export supply
Export sales contract, purchase order, or formal order from the overseas customer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS and Korea Customs Service jointly verify actual export through UNI-PASS records, match the zero-rated e-tax invoice with the export declaration, and confirm that export proceeds were repatriated to Korea in foreign currency. If the zero-rating is disallowed due to absence of valid customs clearance, unrepatriated foreign exchange beyond the 180-day deadline without an approved extension, false e-tax invoice coding, or fabricated export documentation, NTS will retroactively assess 10% VAT on the export value, add statutory late-payment interest and additional tax for false or non-issued tax invoices, and claw back input VAT previously refunded. Fraudulent schemes are also referred under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and may result in criminal fines, imprisonment, and personal exposure for the responsible officers of the Yuhan Hoesa.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (The Central Bank of the Republic of Korea) and the Ministry of Economy and Finance as the Foreign Exchange Administration
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates under a managed floating exchange rate system but statutory foreign exchange controls under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Current account transactions, such as trade in goods and services, are generally liberalized and can be settled through authorized foreign exchange banks; payment for exports must be received within three months of exportation, unless extended by bank approval. Capital account transactions, including foreign direct investment, portfolio flows, and loans, are subject to a notification or approval regime with specific reporting through foreign exchange banks or the Ministry of Economy and Finance. There is no mandatory surrender of export foreign currency proceeds into Korean won, provided the exporter maintains a foreign currency account at a domestic foreign exchange bank; however, all receipts must be repatriated to South Korea within the statutory timeline. Profit remittance in the form of dividends is permitted after corporate tax settlement, but requires proof of tax payment, audited financial statements, and board resolution confirming distributable reserves. Foreign exchange banks verify the underlying trade documents and assign a foreign exchange classification code. For Korean LLCs with non-resident shareholders, dividend remittance is generally possible via SWIFT MT103 once the bank compliance team clears the beneficial ownership profile. The capital account remains selectively controlled, so all inward direct investments must be notified to the designated foreign exchange bank and reported to the Ministry of Economy and Finance through the Foreign Investment Promotion Act before any capital inflow can be converted. Convertibility of the Korean won is limited for speculative purposes but fully supported for genuine trade, dividend, and repatriation flows, provided documentary evidence and tax compliance are demonstrated. The practical hurdle is not the absence of convertibility but the heavy documentary burden imposed by the foreign exchange bank in aligning the transaction with the statutory foreign exchange classification code and beneficial ownership verification standards.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, export receipts must be received and repatriated within three months from the date of exportation (customs clearance); the Korean exporter may retain 100% in a designated foreign currency account and no statutory conversion ratio to Korean won is imposed, but the bank must be notified and the receipt must be deposited to the foreign currency account with matching export documentation such as the invoice, packing list, and customs declaration.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW and USD)
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Current Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to nil for offshore fintech EMIs. South Korea's Foreign Exchange Transactions Act requires cross-border payment and deposit-taking services to be executed by domestic foreign exchange banks. Offshore fintech EMIs such as Wise, Payoneer, and global virtual account providers are not licensed as foreign exchange banks in Korea and cannot legally provide payable accounts or settlement rails for this Korean LLC. A limited passporting possibility exists under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act only for registered domestic e-money institutions, but those companies still cannot provide foreign exchange clearing rails without a sponsorship arrangement with a Tier-1 chartered commercial bank. Attempting to route inbound capital or export proceeds through an EMI would create a reportable unapproved foreign exchange transaction and trigger immediate regulatory scrutiny. The KYC underwriting team should therefore disregard EMI proposals and require the entity to open all corporate accounts directly with a domestic foreign exchange bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For non-resident shareholders and foreign statutory directors, a physical in-branch visit by the authorized representative is normally mandatory for initial corporate account opening. Remote documentary opening is only accepted if the company has a locally resident director holding an original power of attorney, with notarized and Apostilled constitutional documents, passport copies, business license, and beneficial ownership declarations. Some Tier-1 banks allow a video KYC interview for the non-resident beneficial owner after the local representative has appeared in person, but the final approval rests with the bank's AML committee. Since this entity is a Korean LLC with non-resident ownership allowed and a high-value medical device manufacturing scope, expecting at least one statutory director or a locally appointed representative to attend a physical branch session is the most prudent underwriting assumption. Consular proxy opening is not broadly accepted in South Korea; most banks require local presence or a notarized power of attorney suitable for use in Korea.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear economic substance or chain-of-title from final beneficial owners, especially when the Korean LLC is held through an intermediate holding company in Hong Kong or Singapore.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a certified group structure chart signed by the ultimate shareholder, certificates of incorporation and register of directors/shareholders for all intermediate entities, Companies Registry or ACRA filings, notarized passports of all UBOs holding 10% or more, and audited financial statements of the parent or significant shareholder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent invoicing or exposure to dual-use medical technology end-user risk under UN sanctions and Korea's Foreign Trade Act.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide an end-user certificate from the final hospital or distributor, purchase orders referencing the specific DR flat panel detectors, full transportation documents, and evidence of the company's internal export control screening against US BIS Entity List, EU consolidated sanctions, and UN Security Council resolutions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Funds source cannot be evidenced for the inbound capital injection into the Korean LLC.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a board resolution authorizing the capital contribution, a signed source-of-funds statement from the shareholder, recent bank statements of the investing entity, evidence of corporate income tax payment or dividend declarations, and the tax identification number certificate of the investing company.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Recent change in directors or shareholding within the prior 12 months, creating historic identity verification gaps.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit official chronological registry extracts from the Korean Registry, certified translations, notarized resignation and acceptance documents, and a written explanation letter from the current directors. Include a declaration that no politically exposed person has been appointed during the past year.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For non-resident equity investment in a Korean LLC, the investor must report the foreign direct investment to the designated Foreign Exchange Bank under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The capital must be wired via SWIFT MT103 to a foreign currency account at a domestic foreign exchange bank using the Foreign Exchange Classification Code for direct investment; the bank will issue a certificate of capital verification. The funds may be converted to Korean won at the closing spot rate and deposited into the corporate won account. All inbound remittances must be tagged with the FD purpose code, and any loan or equity injection exceeding KRW regulatory thresholds must be reported to the Ministry of Economy and Finance within the specified statutory timeline. The source of funds must be evidenced through audited financial statements or documented retained earnings to pass the bank's enhanced due diligence.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade disbursements for radiology components should be settled via SWIFT MT103 for open account transactions, documentary collections (DP/DA) through the foreign exchange bank for confirmed purchase orders, and commercial letters of credit for non-established counterparties. All settlements require submission of the commercial invoice, bill of lading or airway bill, packing list, and customs declarations to the foreign exchange bank. For supply of vapor deposition equipment and imported cesium iodide crystals from Japan or China, a back-to-back letter of credit structure may be used to mitigate counterparty risk. The bank will perform a transaction-level foreign exchange review and assign the appropriate trade classification code before outward remittance is released. Companies are required to maintain complete export and import settlement records for at least five years under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, and any discrepancy between the invoice amount and the remittance currency must be justified with supporting evidence.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Delivery-versus-payment foreign exchange forward contracts with tenors up to five years for underlying trade commitments
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed with licensed domestic banks referencing KRW or offshore CNH for eligible hedgers with verified underlying exposure

Currency options and cross-currency swaps, including FX swaps and cross-currency interest rate swaps, permitted for managing balance-sheet currency exposure under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting package comprising approved financial statements, business report, directors' report, statutory auditor's report (if any), and signed AGM minutes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company registered head office; meeting minutes and financial statements retained in statutory minute book and available for inspection by members, creditors, court-appointed inspectors, and tax authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa, no later than March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the AGM or to prepare and retain approved financial statements may invalidate the corporate tax filing extension, expose directors to administrative fines of up to KRW 5,000,000 under the Commercial Act, and support court-ordered dissolution of a dormant company after five consecutive years of no business activity

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Final Return and supporting tax schedules for the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of South Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year company, by March 31; automatically extended to May 31 for companies subject to mandatory external audit or where audited financial statements are required for reliable tax reporting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or late-filing penalty of 20% of the assessed corporate tax, underreporting penalty of 10%, and a daily late-payment surcharge of approximately 0.025% from the statutory due date until full payment; persistent tax delinquency triggers NTS asset seizure, cancellation of business registration, and administrative dissolution of the dormant company

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax Return (municipal/provincial surtax on national corporate tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government where the registered head office is located; filed through the local tax electronic system (Wetax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the same corporate tax filing window; for calendar-year companies, by March 31, with matching extension to May 31 for audited entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Local tax surcharges for erroneous or omitted returns (up to 10-20% of the local tax due), daily delinquent interest, seizure of bank accounts and corporate assets, and administrative enforcement measures leading to strike-off of a persistently non-filing company

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent Certified Public Accountant (CPA) External Audit Report on annual financial statements, including balance sheet, income statement, and cash flow statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) under the External Audit Act, with a copy attached to the NTS corporate tax file where audit is mandatory
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit must be completed and presented to the members before the AGM; for a calendar-year company, by March 31, or by May 31 where the audited-company tax extension applies; the signed audit report is lodged with the FSS through the external audit reporting system within two weeks after the AGM
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an external auditor or submit the audit report may invalidate the May 31 tax extension, expose directors and auditors to administrative fines up to KRW 50,000,000, and allow the FSS to order a special inspection or audit designation at company expense; misstatements may trigger statutory auditor liability

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Change Report and annual update of foreign-owned shareholding/beneficial ownership confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through KOTRA or the designated Korean foreign exchange bank; copy retained in the Foreign Investment Enterprise registration file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Any share transfer, contribution increase or decrease, or change of foreign investor details must be reported within 30 days of the event; annual status confirmation is aligned with the annual corporate tax filing by March 31 for calendar-year foreign-invested companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Untimely or omitted Foreign Investment Promotion Act and Foreign Exchange Transactions Act reports may result in fines up to KRW 10,000,000, loss of foreign-investment legal protections, denial of tax treaty benefits under limitation-on-benefits analysis, and administrative cancellation of the foreign investment enterprise registration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner/UBO confirmation and on-site statutory register audit certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company head office and registered agent; records must be available to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU), financial institutions performing customer due diligence, and the National Tax Service on request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually no later than the AGM date; any change in membership interests, control, or UBO must be recorded and, if a non-resident is involved, reported within the 30-day statutory change window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or confirm UBO and statutory register records may expose directors to Commercial Act administrative fines, AML/CFT compliance fines imposed by KoFIU, and loss of evidentiary presumption of statutory register accuracy

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Korean External Audit Act, an independent certified CPA audit is compulsory for a non-listed Yuhan Hoesa if total assets at fiscal year-end equal or exceed KRW 12,000,000,000. The Financial Services Commission may also designate a company for mandatory external audit where total assets are KRW 7,000,000,000 or more and designation criteria exist, including annual revenue exceeding KRW 10,000,000,000, an average workforce of 100 or more employees, or public-interest circumstances such as participation with listed companies, financial institutions, or NTS referral. Headcount alone does not automatically trigger an audit for a private LLC, and no SME turnover threshold can override the asset-based statutory trigger. Once triggered, the audit must cover the complete balance sheet, income statement, statement of changes in equity, and statement of cash flows.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korea International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) as adopted by the Korean Accounting Standards Board; alternatively, Korean GAAP (General Corporate Accounting Standards) for non-listed companies; small and medium-size entities may apply the Korean Accounting Standards for Small and Medium Entities. Audit engagements must be performed under Korean Auditing Standards, which are aligned with International Standards on Auditing.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Yuhan Hoesa must obtain a written annual confirmation of beneficial and registered ownership from every member before the AGM and before any dividend payment. The confirmation must identify the natural person ultimately owning or controlling 10% or more of the entity, the direct member, any nominee/trust arrangement, and any non-resident individual or entity with a reportable interest. Any transfer of membership interests, change in ownership percentages, or change in control/UBO must be updated in the statutory register immediately and reported within 30 days where a foreign investor or foreign exchange reporting event is involved. The relationship bank and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) may require the refreshed UBO record during customer due diligence or AML/CFT inspection.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (including a beneficial ownership annex for each member and UBO)
Minutes of Members' Meetings and Board Meetings (Minute Book)
Accounting ledgers, books of account, and corporate tax records retained for at least 7 years

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 - USD 1,500 per year for a standard Seoul/business hub registered office and company secretary; USD 2,500 - USD 5,000 per year for foreign-lawyer-assisted corporate secretarial, local agent, and annual compliance management services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - USD 25,000 per year for a Tier-2 Korean CPA firm statutory audit of a small to medium-size LLC; USD 30,000 or more where K-IFRS, FSS designation, or consolidated group reporting applies

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Progressive national Corporate Income Tax: 9% up to KRW 200 million; 19% from KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion; 21% from KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion; 24% above KRW 300 billion, plus 10% local corporate income tax surcharge on the national tax (combined top statutory effective rate of 26.4%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Available incentives under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act include R&D tax credits for high-tech manufacturing, tax credits for capital investment in new growth engine technologies, Free Economic Zone and Foreign Investment Zone holiday/reduction benefits, and partial tax exemptions for technology transfer and patent income derived from qualifying Korean IP. A digital X-ray flat-panel OEM manufacturing in Korea may be eligible for R&D and facility investment credits, but free-zone incentives require actual Korean headquarters and manufacturing substance.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Standard Corporate Income Tax Return on Tax Base and Tax Calculation - Annual Corporate Tax Return, filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax portal (www.hometax.go.kr), including all supplementary schedules for foreign-related transactions, non-resident withholding, and tax credits.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with a mandatory first-half interim prepayment filing for all Korean corporations)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return must be filed and tax paid within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year company, the deadline is March 31. First-half interim prepayment is due within 2 months after the end of the first half of the fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 1a - Gross Revenue and Operating Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report total worldwide gross revenue and ordinary business income of the Korean limited liability company, adjusted under Korean GAAP / K-IFRS.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all Korean-source and foreign-source commercial income. Do not exclude export sales of digital X-ray flat-panel detectors merely because the customer is a non-resident related distributor. If the foreign related distributor is a limited-risk buy-sell distributor, the Korean manufacturer must book the arm's-length export price; any year-end transfer-pricing adjustment must be reflected and supported by a benchmarking study.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 1b - Non-Deductible Expenses and Related-Party Charges
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report statutory disallowances, including excessive entertainment expense, non-deductible penalties, related-party payments not satisfying arm's-length principles, and secret fund indicators.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees, technological service fees, and royalty payments payable to a non-resident controlling shareholder are deductible only when actual services are rendered, the fees are supported by contracts and records, and the character of payment is established ahead of payment. A non-resident beneficial owner must file the treaty relief package with the Korean payor before the payment; otherwise, 22% withholding applies, and the Korean entity must not record a tax credit for the non-resident's tax obligation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Related-Party Interest Deduction Limitation / Thin Capitalization
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjust deductible interest for loans from foreign controlling shareholders under Korea's thin capitalization rule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where the loan from a controlling non-resident shareholder and other foreign related parties exceeds three times the Korean entity's equity investment, excess interest is non-deductible. State all cross-border debt in the international tax adjustment schedule; list lender, relationship, debt-to-equity ratio, and applicable treaty interest withholding rate. Failure to disclose creates a red flag for hidden equity or disguised profit repatriation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Taxable Income before Loss Carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute taxable income after Korean GAAP adjustments, non-deductible expenses, tax-free income, special deductions, and thin-capitalization disallowances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This line must capture all foreign adjustments including transfer-pricing corrections. If a non-resident shareholder receives a dividend, royalty, or interest payment from the Korean entity after the balance-sheet date, that amount is not deducted from taxable income; it is a separately taxed profit repatriation subject to 20% national withholding plus 2% local surcharge, unless a DTA provides a reduced rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 4 - Tax Credits and Foreign Tax Credit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter credits for foreign taxes paid by the Korean company on income earned through a PE or through direct foreign operations, plus domestic R&D and employment credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The foreign tax credit belongs to the Korean resident entity and cannot be used to offset withholding taxes owed on behalf of non-resident shareholders. In an IP-heavy OEM relationship, royalties paid by the Korean entity are subject to Korean source withholding at treaty rates; any foreign tax withheld abroad should be reported here only if it is genuinely Korean-source income assessed to the Korean entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 5 - National Corporate Tax, Local Surtax, and Net Tax Due
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate final national corporate tax, add 10% local corporate income tax surcharge, deduct prepayments, and state the final amount payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Before distributing after-tax profits to a non-resident shareholder, the Korean company must settle the annual corporate tax liability in full. The non-resident dividend withholding is a separate post-balance-sheet obligation for the Korean paying company as withholding agent; the company must file the monthly Flat-Rate Tax Withholding Return for non-resident income by the 10th day of the following month and pay the home/local withholding taxes.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing and late payment expose the company to penalty taxes under the Framework Act on National Taxes: non-filing penalty tax of 20% of the tax unpaid; under-reporting penalty tax of 10% of the insufficiently reported amount; fraudulent/aggressive non-reporting penalty tax of 40% of the evaded amount; unpaid tax penalty is 1.2% per month. Ministerial daily surcharges and interest on underpaid national tax apply. Where tax evasion or intentional non-declaration exceeds KRW 300 million, the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act allows referral to a public prosecutor with possible imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to five times the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Statutory withholding on cash dividends paid to a non-resident is 20% national income tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge (22% aggregate), absent a Korea DTA.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a DTA reduced rate, the Korean paying company must obtain, before settlement, the non-resident shareholder's Tax Residency Certificate issued by the foreign competent authority, plus a Korea-dated Beneficial Ownership Statement confirming the payee is the true owner, receives the income for its own benefit, and has no obligation to pass the income to another person. The Korean withholding agent submits the treaty application and supporting certificate to the National Tax Service with the withholding return; if the higher 22% is withheld because treaty documents are late, the non-resident must file a domestic tax refund claim and obtain a treaty-based re-categorization within the statutory limit of 4 years from the filing deadline.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties for IP, technical assistance, and know-how paid to a non-resident are statutorily subject to 20% national withholding plus 2% local surcharge; interest on foreign related-party loans is also statutorily subject to 20% plus 2% local surcharge. Under recent Korean treaties, interest and royalty rates are generally reduced to 10-15%; dividends are generally reduced to 5-15% depending on shareholding percentages and beneficial ownership. The reduced rate is not automatic; the recipient must satisfy treaty-limitation-on-benefits clauses, demonstrate Korean business substance, and provide the TRC and beneficial ownership form before the payment date.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File preparation is triggered when aggregate foreign-related transaction value with Korean overseas related parties exceeds KRW 50 billion; Master File is required when such transactions exceed KRW 100 billion; Country-by-Country Report applies to multinational groups with consolidated revenue above KRW 1 trillion. Even below thresholds, a contemporaneous Local File is prudent whenever the digital X-ray flat-panel manufacturing company has intercompany export sales, royalty payments, or management fees.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea follows the substance-over-form principle and applies Controlled Foreign Company rules under the International Tax Adjustment Act. A Korean entity cannot be treated as a mere invoice operator or limited-risk shell unless its assets, functions, and risks are contractually and factually allocated in accordance with the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines. The Core Income-Generating Activities for a medical-device OEM include design control, regulatory licensing, manufacturing, quality assurance, and logistics decision-making; these must be carried out in Korea with real personnel and assets. Excessive profit diversion to low-tax beach-head entities will be recharacterized and penalized.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional omission of foreign export revenue from digital X-ray flat-panel detectors, creation of fictitious purchase invoices for component procurement, or under-reporting of taxable income through secret foreign bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, aggravated tax evasion exceeding KRW 300 million is punishable by imprisonment of up to 5 years and a fine of up to five times the evaded tax. Under the Framework Act on National Taxes, fraudulent under-reporting triggers a penalty tax of 40% of the underpaid amount plus monthly arrears charges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The representative director who signed the fraudulent return may be jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax under Article 39 of the National Tax Collection Act; personal bank accounts and assets can be seized; where unpaid tax exceeds KRW 50 million, the tax authority may request a departure restriction (travel ban) preventing the director from leaving Korea; criminal conviction can bar the director from serving as an officer.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Abuse and Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Booking management fees or royalty payments to an offshore related company that lacks personnel, premises, management, or actual decision-making authority while the Korean subsidiary performs all Core Income-Generating Activities, or pricing intercompany export sales below cost to shift profit to a low-tax jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The National Tax Service will apply the arm's-length method under Articles 4 and 5 of the International Tax Adjustment Act, adjust taxable income, disallow excess deductions, and impose penalty tax for undisclosed or incorrectly reported foreign-related transactions, generally 30% of the amount adjusted where intentional non-disclosure is found. A criminal referral is possible if the arrangement is characterized as fraudulent avoidance of tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approved the transfer pricing structure can be personally assessed as promoters under Article 39 of the National Tax Collection Act; they are jointly and severally liable for the company's resulting tax if they acted as de facto principals; under Korean Commercial Act Article 401 they may owe civil damages for injury to creditors; the tax authority may freeze assets and impose an overseas travel suspension on the director.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Evasion and Disguised Profit Repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest, or royalties to a non-resident shareholder without withholding the statutory 20% national tax and 2% local surcharge, or mislabeling true royalties as routine offline service payments to avoid Korean-source withholding, or using a conduit entity to claim treaty relief without economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Korean paying company, as withholding agent, is liable for the un-withheld tax and penalty tax under the Framework Act on National Taxes: 20% of the un-withheld tax for willful failure, 10% for negligent failure, plus monthly late payment surcharges. If treaty relief is denied, the entire national/local withholding tax becomes immediately collectable, with interest, from the Korean entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The representative director is personally liable for withheld taxes collected but not remitted to the National Tax Service under Article 39 of the National Tax Collection Act; the amount can be recovered directly from the director's personal property. Willful suppression of cross-border payments can be prosecuted as embezzlement of national tax under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, with imprisonment up to 5 years; departure blacklisting and asset attachment are standard collection remedies against the director.
